documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, tax identification number, bank reference letter or statements, source-of-funds/income evidence; some banks ask for local ties.
min_deposit_fees: Consultancy sources cite opening deposits from about USD 10,000 depending on account type; bank fees not published for non-residents.
banks: CIBC Caribbean (FirstCaribbean), RBC Royal Bank, Republic Bank, First Citizens, Sagicor Bank; acceptance of non-residents varies by bank and profile.
restrictions: Heavy KYC/CRS and FATCA reporting; many banks require economic ties to Barbados; Barbados exchange controls apply to BBD accounts, foreign-currency accounts need approval.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for multi-currency needs; offshore/international banks in Barbados for higher-net-worth clients.
cost_note: Consultancy sources cite opening deposits from about USD 10,000 (already USD) depending on bank and account type; no Barbadian bank publishes a non-resident opening or monthly fee, so those are null.

documents: Passport or ID, residence permit (often), proof of address, completed application; diaspora remote openings use notarized signatures by mail.
min_deposit_fees: US trade guide cites a minimum deposit of HTG 2,500 for individual accounts; fees not published.
banks: Unibank (diaspora account-from-abroad process reported), Sogebank, BNC; non-resident foreigner acceptance case-by-case.
restrictions: Severe security crisis and gang violence disrupt branches; correspondent-banking de-risking limits USD transfers; strict AML checks.
alternatives: Mobile money (MonCash, Natcash) requires local SIM/ID; remittance services such as Western Union or Remitly for sending funds.
cost_note: US trade guide cites a minimum deposit of HTG 2,500 for individual accounts (about USD 19 at roughly HTG 131 = USD 1); opening and monthly fees are not published by Unibank, Sogebank or BNC.

documents: Passport plus, at most banks, cedula de extranjeria (requires visa over 3 months), Colombian address and phone, proof of income; branch visit required.
min_deposit_fees: Personal accounts reported from about USD 50 initial deposit; non-resident fees not published.
banks: Bancolombia and Davivienda generally require cedula; BBVA Colombia reportedly opens some accounts in person with passport only.
restrictions: SARLAFT AML screening lets banks refuse non-residents; foreign-exchange registration rules (Banco de la Republica) for inbound funds; 4x1000 financial transactions tax.
alternatives: Nequi and Daviplata digital wallets accept passports with low limits; Wise or Revolut for international transfers.
cost_note: Personal accounts are reported to open with about USD 50 initial deposit (secondary sources, roughly COP 200,000 at COP 4,000 = USD 1); Bancolombia, Davivienda and BBVA Colombia do not publish non-resident opening or monthly fees.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, bank reference letter, proof of income and source of funds; some private banks also want a local tax ID and Uruguayan phone.
min_deposit_fees: BROU reportedly requires new non-resident foreigners to place a USD 5,000 fixed-term deposit for 181 days; Santander non-resident accounts carry high minimum balances (amount not published).
banks: Banco Republica (BROU), Itau Uruguay (non-resident account), Santander Uruguay (online non-resident account), Scotiabank (in person).
restrictions: No capital controls and USD accounts widely available; strict source-of-funds checks and CRS/FATCA reporting; non-resident accounts may face higher fees.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; Prex and Mi Dinero cards for locals with cedula.
cost_note: BROU non-resident foreigner page: USD 5,000 fixed-term deposit for 181 days, client registration 300 UI plus savings-account opening 150 UI (450 UI, about UYU 2,900) and a non-waivable monthly fee of 150 UI (about UYU 960), at roughly UYU 6.4 per UI and UYU 40 = USD 1.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, proof of income/source of funds, account purpose; some banks ask for a Macau non-resident worker (Blue) card.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Bank of China Macau, BNU (Banco Nacional Ultramarino), ICBC Macau; acceptance of non-residents varies by bank and branch.
restrictions: No legal bar on foreigners, but in-person visit is required and banks apply strict AML due to the gaming sector; MOP pegged to HKD, no capital controls.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut; Hong Kong banks for a nearby multi-currency option.
cost_note: Bank of China Macau, BNU and ICBC Macau do not publish non-resident personal account opening fees, minimum deposits or monthly fees, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport with a valid long-stay visa (3-6 months or more), proof of local address, employer or embassy letter or investment-commission recommendation.
min_deposit_fees: Historical minimums of USD 100-1,000 depending on purpose; current figures not published.
banks: none known for non-residents; KBZ Bank, CB Bank, AYA Bank serve resident foreigners.
restrictions: FATF blacklist (call for action), US/EU/Australian sanctions on military-linked banks (MFTB, MICB), currency controls and forced FX conversion, no interest paid to foreigners.
alternatives: none practical; foreigners rely on offshore accounts in Thailand or Singapore.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts in Myanmar, so no cost applies (historical resident-foreigner minimums of USD 100-1,000 are not current).

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, bank reference, source-of-funds evidence, completed application taken to a branch.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: ANZ Vanuatu, BRED Bank Vanuatu, Bank South Pacific (BSP) Vanuatu, National Bank of Vanuatu; non-resident acceptance case-by-case.
restrictions: Formerly on EU/FATF grey lists, causing correspondent de-risking; banks restrict non-residents tied to the citizenship-by-investment programme.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut; Australian or NZ bank account for regional transfers.
cost_note: ANZ, BRED, BSP and National Bank of Vanuatu do not publish non-resident personal account opening fees, minimum deposits or monthly fees, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport (sometimes notarized Armenian translation), local or temporary address, phone number; occasionally purpose of account or source-of-funds proof.
min_deposit_fees: Opening often free to about AMD 10,000; monthly fees not published.
banks: Ameriabank, Ardshinbank, ACBA Bank, Inecobank, Evocabank; most require a first in-person identification for foreign non-residents.
restrictions: Enhanced due diligence for some nationalities (notably post-2022 Russian inflows); banks do not use IBAN; sanctions screening.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut; Armenian bank mobile apps once onboarded.
cost_note: Armenian banks such as Ameriabank (which advertises a free Smart account) typically open personal accounts free or for up to about AMD 10,000 (about USD 26 at AMD 390 = USD 1); minimum deposits and monthly fees for non-residents are not published.

documents: Biometric passport or consular card plus valid residence card, proof of local address, initial deposit; in-branch opening in Bangui only.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-residents; Ecobank Centrafrique, BSIC Centrafrique, Banque Populaire Maroco-Centrafricaine serve residents.
restrictions: Conflict and security risk; CEMAC/BEAC foreign-exchange regulations restrict foreign-currency accounts; correspondent de-risking; UN arms embargo and sanctions on individuals.
alternatives: Orange Money or Moov mobile money with local SIM; Cameroon-based CEMAC banks.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts in the Central African Republic, so no cost applies and none is published.

documents: Passport plus long-term visa, work permit or residence certificate at most banks; local address, TIN for some accounts, passport photos.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Stanbic Bank Uganda, Absa Bank Uganda, Standard Chartered Uganda; foreigners with only a short-term visa are commonly refused.
restrictions: Bank of Uganda KYC rules tie accounts to lawful stay; remote diaspora accounts are for Ugandan nationals only; FX accounts in USD available.
alternatives: MTN MoMo or Airtel Money with a registered SIM (needs passport and visa); Wise or Revolut for transfers.
cost_note: Stanbic, Absa and Standard Chartered Uganda do not publish non-resident personal account costs, and short-term visitors are commonly refused, so all figures are null.

documents: Certified passport, work or residence permit, Botswana proof of residence (utility bill), proof of income; non-resident files case-by-case.
min_deposit_fees: Absa Botswana personal accounts cite minimum income of BWP 750; non-resident deposits/fees not published.
banks: Absa Bank Botswana, FNB Botswana, Stanbic Bank Botswana, Standard Chartered Botswana, First Capital Bank; none confirmed to onboard non-residents remotely.
restrictions: No exchange controls (abolished 1999) and foreign-currency accounts available, but strict KYC tied to local residence.
alternatives: Orange Money or MyZaka mobile money with local SIM; South African bank non-resident accounts; Wise or Revolut.
cost_note: Absa Botswana cites a minimum income of BWP 750 (about USD 55 at BWP 13.6 = USD 1), which is an eligibility test not a deposit; no Botswana bank publishes non-resident opening, deposit or monthly fees.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, proof of income, foreign tax identification number; some banks require an existing EU/French IBAN for the first deposit.
min_deposit_fees: Non-resident accounts often carry higher monthly fees and minimum deposits; amounts not published consistently.
banks: BNP Paribas (non-resident/expat service), Societe Generale (branch discretion), CIC and Credit Agricole regional banks for property buyers; Boursobank is mostly resident-only.
restrictions: No capital controls; CRS/FATCA reporting; non-resident accounts usually lack overdrafts and credit; Banque de France 'droit au compte' covers residents of France (and certain EU cases) only.
alternatives: N26, Revolut, bunq or Wise for EUR IBANs opened remotely.
cost_note: BNP Paribas, Societe Generale and regional banks charge non-residents higher monthly fees and deposits but do not publish consistent non-resident amounts, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport plus second photo ID, for non-EU citizens often a residence permit or proof of Czech connection (lease, employment, study), Czech phone number.
min_deposit_fees: Some banks ask for an opening deposit of CZK 100-1,000; non-resident fees not published.
banks: Fio banka and Raiffeisenbank sometimes open in branch; Air Bank reportedly no longer opens for foreigners; acceptance case-by-case.
restrictions: Online opening requires Czech bank ID or residence; banks may refuse non-EU non-residents without local ties; standard EU AML/CRS rules.
alternatives: Revolut, Wise, N26 (EUR) and similar EU fintechs.
cost_note: Fio banka advertises its personal account as free (no opening or monthly fee, CZK 0); other banks may ask an opening deposit of CZK 100-1,000 (about USD 4-43 at CZK 23 = USD 1) and a Fio minimum deposit is not published.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, stated purpose of account; some banks want apostilled documents or an Albanian residence permit.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Credins Bank (in-branch KYC with passport), Raiffeisen Bank Albania (online only for residents), BKT; policies vary by branch.
restrictions: Albania removed from FATF grey list in 2023 but banks remain cautious; several banks refuse non-Albanians without residence permit.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut; Albanian residence permit route for full banking.
cost_note: Credins, Raiffeisen Albania and BKT do not publish non-resident personal account opening fees, minimum deposits or monthly fees, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport plus second ID at some banks, proof of foreign address, all certified by a solicitor or police officer and in English; PPS number not needed for non-residents.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Bank of Ireland (non-resident account, certified documents by post), AIB (contact form, branch ID check within 30 days); PTSB mostly resident-only.
restrictions: No capital controls; CRS/FATCA reporting; banks often expect an Irish link such as property purchase; few remaining full-service banks after Ulster Bank and KBC exits.
alternatives: Revolut (Irish-licensed bank with IE IBANs for EEA residents), Wise, N26 or bunq.
cost_note: Bank of Ireland and AIB do not publish separate non-resident account opening fees, minimum deposits or maintenance fees in the sources gathered, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport, questionnaire on account purpose and Lithuanian connection, income and source-of-funds proof; some banks require a residence permit.
min_deposit_fees: Swedbank charges an administration fee for non-EU residents; SEB charges higher monthly fees to non-residents; opening fees reported up to EUR 400.
banks: SEB, Swedbank, Luminor, Artea Bankas (formerly Siauliu bankas); acceptance of non-EU non-residents is case-by-case.
restrictions: Very strict compliance after Baltic money-laundering scandals; banks often refuse non-residents without local ties; sanctions screening for Russia/Belarus links.
alternatives: Lithuanian-licensed EMIs and Revolut Bank UAB offer LT IBANs remotely; Wise, Paysera.
cost_note: Swedbank and SEB charge non-EU residents an administration fee and higher monthly fees, with opening fees reported up to EUR 400 (about USD 465 at USD 1.16 = EUR 1), but no bank publishes a definitive non-resident figure, so values are null.

documents: Passport, Iraqi residency card, salary attestation or employer letter, compliance clearance; in-branch visit required.
min_deposit_fees: Varies by bank; Byblos Bank Iraq term deposits from USD 20,000; current-account minimums not published.
banks: none known for non-residents; Byblos Bank Iraq, Rafidain and Rasheed (state) and Kurdistan private banks serve residents.
restrictions: US Federal Reserve-driven USD restrictions and bans on many Iraqi banks for dollar transactions; strict CBI KYC; security risks; cash-heavy economy.
alternatives: Zain Cash, Qi Card and FIB (First Iraqi Bank app) need local ID; Western Union for transfers.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts in Iraq, so no cost applies (Byblos Bank Iraq term deposits from USD 20,000 are for eligible residents).

documents: Passport with valid entry visa, proof of address, local mobile number, source of funds; many branches still ask for a residence or work permit.
min_deposit_fees: Initial cash deposit usually required; amounts vary by bank and are not published for non-residents.
banks: National Bank of Egypt, CIB, HSBC Egypt (branch visit with passport and visa); practice varies between branches.
restrictions: CBE circular of August 2024 requires banks to open non-resident accounts for foreigners, but with full KYC; FX repatriation and withdrawal documentation rules; currency volatility.
alternatives: InstaPay and mobile wallets (Vodafone Cash) need a local account or SIM; Wise for transfers.
cost_note: National Bank of Egypt, CIB and HSBC Egypt require an initial cash deposit but do not publish amounts or monthly fees for non-residents, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport and proof of residence for in-branch opening in Asmara; no published non-resident procedure.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-residents; Commercial Bank of Eritrea (state-owned) is the only full retail bank.
restrictions: Strict currency controls, nakfa withdrawal limits, foreign currency must be exchanged at official rate; isolated banking system with minimal correspondent links.
alternatives: none; Wise and remittance services have very limited coverage.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts in Eritrea, so no cost applies and the Commercial Bank of Eritrea publishes no tariff.

documents: Passport, visa, proof of purpose of stay or employment, photographs, KYC form; NFCD accounts for foreign nationals per Bangladesh Bank FE rules.
min_deposit_fees: A secondary guide cites USD 25,000 minimum for foreign-national NFCD accounts; ordinary account fees not published.
banks: Standard Chartered Bangladesh, HSBC Bangladesh, Eastern Bank and other authorized dealer banks; non-resident foreigner acceptance not confirmed.
restrictions: Foreign exchange regulations restrict taka accounts for non-residents to approved purposes; FX reserve pressure and repatriation controls.
alternatives: bKash or Nagad mobile money require a local SIM and national ID or passport; Wise for inbound transfers.
cost_note: A secondary guide cites a USD 25,000 minimum for foreign-national NFCD accounts (already USD); opening and monthly fees for non-resident foreigners are not published.

documents: Passport, embassy/consular card or carte de sejour (residence permit), proof of local address, TIN if available, initial deposit.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Ecobank Benin, Bank of Africa (BOA) Benin, Orabank; branch visit required and non-resident acceptance case-by-case.
restrictions: BCEAO/WAEMU foreign-exchange regulations limit non-resident accounts in XOF; strict KYC; beware remote-account scams.
alternatives: MTN MoMo or Moov Money with local SIM; Wave; Wise for XOF payouts.
cost_note: Ecobank Benin, BOA Benin and Orabank do not publish non-resident personal account opening fees, minimum deposits or monthly fees, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport, proof of address or residence, residence permit if applicable, TIN if available, passport photos, initial deposit; in-branch KYC.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Ecobank Liberia, LBDI, Afriland First Bank, GT Bank Liberia; no bank confirmed to open personal accounts remotely for non-residents.
restrictions: Dual USD/LRD economy; correspondent-banking de-risking; Central Bank of Liberia KYC rules; in-person presence usually required.
alternatives: Orange Money or MTN Lonestar MoMo with local SIM; Western Union/MoneyGram for transfers.
cost_note: Ecobank Liberia, LBDI, Afriland and GT Bank Liberia do not publish non-resident personal account opening fees, minimum deposits or monthly fees, so all figures are null.
